Leaf candidates narrowed to 19 classes. Top candidates: Northern_Leaf_Blight, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Goss_S_Wilt. Now viewing one reference per class.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Large, elongated/spindle-shaped lesion on a corn leaf. Tan/grayish center with very prominent dark reddish-brown to purple margins. Some yellowing around the lesion.

- **NLB reference**: Cigar-shaped tan lesions, more uniformly colored without the prominent dark margins seen in the test image.

- **SCLB reference**: Smaller, more rectangular lesions with reddish-brown margins — doesn't match the size or shape in the test image.

- **Anthracnose reference**: Oval/spindle-shaped lesions with tan centers and dark brown/purple margins — closely matches the test image pattern. Description also notes lesions can enlarge to 5–6 inches.

- **Goss's Wilt reference**: Large water-soaked blighted areas with wavy margins — clearly different.

The test image most closely matches **Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback**: the prominent dark reddish-brown/purple margins surrounding a tan necrotic center on a large spindle-shaped lesion is the key identifying feature.
